sources.label: Broadsheet — Sundays, a Scroll Micro-Bakery in Bondi
Broadsheet — Everyone's Queuing For the Cinnamon Scrolls at Sundays

blocks.text: Sundays is the tiny micro-bakery at 211 Bondi Road that founder Laetitia Loefti turned into a genuine phenomenon, largely by filming the whole thing on Instagram. On a good day the case can clear within about an hour of opening. So getting a scroll without losing your morning to a line really comes down to three moves: check they're actually open, get there before the doors do, and know your order before you reach the window.

items.label: Golden rule
items.value: Arrive before opening — they sell out

blocks.title: Check the day, then beat the doors
blocks.text: Sundays trades a limited number of days a week and the schedule has shifted since it opened, so old listings disagree — open @sundaysbondi the night before to confirm they're baking. Then treat the posted close as a maximum, not a promise: opening weekend sold out inside the first hour, so being there before opening is the difference between the first batch and no batch.

The scrolls aren't the dense, heavy bakery kind — they're light and almost pancake-like, because each batch of dough is cold-fermented overnight and then left to rise twice more before baking. That texture is the whole point, so order at least one classic to see what the fuss is about.

items: Classic cinnamon with cream cheese — the signature, and the one that goes first. Order it first.
Biscoff — a core flavour, richer and more caramelised if you like things sweeter.
Kinder chocolate — the other regular, and a hit with kids.
Rotating specials like pistachio — these vanish fastest, so grab one if it's on.
Matcha twists and the coconut cloud coffee (whipped espresso over coconut water) — Sundays leans hard into both, and either makes the classic pairing with your scroll.

blocks.text: Seating is tiny to non-existent, so I always get mine takeaway and walk it down to the promenade. A warm cinnamon scroll on the grass above the sand, coffee in hand, is one of my favourite cheap-thrill Bondi mornings.

211 Bondi Road sits roughly halfway between Bondi Junction and the beach. The 333 and 380 buses both run the length of Bondi Road between Bondi Junction interchange (which connects to the train line) and the sand, so you can hop off almost at the door — plug '211 Bondi Road' into the Transport for NSW trip planner for live times. Weekend parking here is metered and fiercely contested, so skip the car if you can.

items.q: What days is Sundays Bondi open?
items.a: It's a limited-days micro-bakery and the schedule has changed since opening, with different listings disagreeing — so confirm on their Instagram (@sundaysbondi) the night before rather than trusting an old post.

items.q: What time should I arrive to beat the queue?
items.a: Before opening. The first batch can go fast — opening weekend sold out within about an hour — so being in the line before the doors open gives you the best shot at the full range of flavours.

Start with the classic cinnamon scroll with cream cheese. The core line-up also includes Biscoff and Kinder chocolate, plus rotating specials like pistachio, matcha twists and the coconut cloud coffee.

items.q: How do I get to 211 Bondi Road?
items.a: It's about halfway between Bondi Junction and Bondi Beach on Bondi Road, served by the 333 and 380 buses from Bondi Junction interchange and walkable up from the promenade.
